The algebraic Cech/Mayer-Vietoris form, where the intersection term carries the coupling, is the additivity item (satisfiable-cover-review:2), developed and folded into the cover-generation obstacle. Earlier Cech leads were developed into lem:cover-relative-gluing.

Developed over five reviews: pairs settled by lem:pair-directness-range and prop:overlap-orientation, single directions by end-additivity. The value-side review identifies many-member additivity with its Obstacle, 'cover generation between two halves', so the remainder is a restatement of the open problem.

Developed: flat-covering sunflowers need about (3/2)^k clauses, beyond budget (cor:value-space-dense-covers). Kernel pinning iterated is per-block removal. The coupled-cover review finds that the live obstruction, couplings, 'come from row sums, not from sunflowers'.
The dense-cover review identifies the iterated renormalization flow with per-block removal ('removes capacity-many forms per round at a robustness cost each time'), whose linear ceiling is recorded.

Developed into lem:weak-base-anticoncentration. Below the column-spread scale the image is nearly uniform, and 'beyond it uniformity is impossible', where the obstacle lies. This is a proved limitation, consistent with A1's 'cannot be found by density or spread'.

Developed into prop:oriented-cylinder-repair and tested on h-regular coupling graphs in the overdetermined review. The value-side review proves that adversarial overlap graphs exceed every cylinder budget, so no orientation exists. The column-local framework and its (HJ) hypothesis hold only within capacity, while the open part of A1 lies beyond joint capacity. The untried hyperedge (hypergraph-orientation) extension would also live in that framework, so no open statement remains for it.
Continued as the generic Jordan type lead, then closed: 'pointwise data cannot certify truncated freeness, by the recorded counterexample'. The graded truncated Dade lemma fails in special position.
Used for the capacities c(b) in prop:oriented-cylinder-repair. The trivial sumset bound suffices, and sharper Kneser bounds do not change which families fail. Its application is exhausted.
Same bridge: the super dimension is pointwise and ungraded, so like rank varieties it cannot see the recorded truncated failures. Beyond capacity there is no tensor factorization to semisimplify.

The numerical Kotecky-Preiss condition passed, but the algebraic translation was never tested. The closure says dimension-level expansions reach only the falls half (conj:fill-point-falls), which is itself still open in A3, so the idea still bears on an open statement; the coupling-distributivity argument rules out only the row-freeness half.

older.title: Standard monomials and order shattering (Mészáros–Rónyai, Standard Monomials and Extremal Vector Systems) with a degree-compatible order
older.text: Use the standard-monomial/shattering description of vanishing ideals of Boolean point sets, with a degree-compatible term order, to bound the filtered image of the separated space modulo the selectors and old relations. Concretely: enlarge the dense-head count by cheaply derived additional heads, each reducer carrying an explicit NS certificate, so that the image bound approaches the true Hilbert function while the certificate cost stays inside the PC ceiling. The lex-order control (H_S(1)=4 versus three lex standard monomials) shows the order must respect total degree.
older.reason: Never developed in this form; the shattering idea was later taken up as Anstee–Rónyai–Sali (design support bound, closed for failure-set sizes in sparse-failure-sets) and is still listed untested for gr F^Q in overdetermined-review, so the standard-monomial normal-form use remains open. Deduplicate against that later listing.

older.title: Solving degree versus last fall degree (Caminata–Gorla, Solving degree, last fall degree, and related invariants, Theorem 3.1)
older.text: Caminata–Gorla split the solving degree of a system into its last fall degree and the largest degree of a reduced Gröbner basis for a degree-compatible order. Translated, the PC refutation degree of PHP plus the prefix clauses is controlled by degree falls of the supplied generators, and their regularity results with explicit hypotheses could bound the last fall degree of the homogenized clause system relative to the PHP base. The fixed-degree PC criterion of the marked fat point would be the bridge between the algorithmic invariant and PC degree.
older.reason: Recorded only as orientation in two entries; no later entry reads Theorem 3.1 or tests the translation from last fall degree to the degree-22k Tor-vanishing statement.
older.open_statement: A3, degree: Tor vanishing / no degree fall through 22k

older.title: Semi-regular sequences (Bardet–Faugère–Salvy–Spaenlehauer) for selector systems modulo PHP
older.text: Bardet, Faugère, Salvy and Spaenlehauer analyse Boolean quadratic systems under semi-regularity: the Hilbert series is the truncated product and the first fall comes at the first nonpositive coefficient. Translated, PHP plus the clause tops would behave like a semi-regular system relative to the base, which is conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base; a proof technique or published bound for semi-regularity of Boolean quadrics would turn the heuristic into the A3 theorem. The survey noted the genericity hypotheses are missing for proof-derived selectors.
older.reason: Dismissed in the survey only for missing hypotheses (a scope objection); the idea was later relisted as an outside lead in budget-review (passed as a translation) and its open content is A3 itself. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-budget-review:3.

older.title: Inverse Littlewood–Offord theorems for arrays and permutations (Do–Nguyen–Phan–Tran–Vu; Berger–Berkowitz–Devlin–Vu), in a fixed-prime form
older.text: Inverse Littlewood–Offord theorems say that a sum of random signed coefficients with large point probability forces the coefficients into a structured (low-rank or progression-like) set. Over F_3, the coefficient rectangles of a form under random swaps play the role of the steps; a fixed-prime inverse theorem would classify forms whose residual coefficients fail to equidistribute, giving a structure-versus-randomness split for adversarial blocks. The review screened only real-valued versions and did not import them.
older.reason: Closed in this review only by a scope objection (real-valued hypotheses); later developed in many entries and relisted with finite-field versions (Tao–Vu; Kwan–Sauermann), still bearing on adversarial forms. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-28-dense-cover-review:1 and entry-2026-09-25-universality-review:1.

older.title: Jordan degree type of multiplication by the marked variable z (Altafi–Iarrobino–Macias Marques, Def. 2.8, Prop. 2.19)
older.text: The NS refutation degree is the length of the z-string through 1 in the homogenized presentation algebra A, and the Jordan degree type of multiplication by z records all string lengths via ranks of graded multiplication maps. Lefschetz-type or Jordan-type results for the distinguished element z, or for z on the tensor product of block algebras over the PHP algebra, would control degree falls. The entry warned that Lefschetz theorems need genericity and can fail in fixed small characteristic.
older.reason: Taken up later (jordan-type-literature, jordan-type-lead, Lefschetz leads in equivalence-route-review) but still listed as continuing in later standard reviews; not shown to have no remaining application. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-equivalence-route-review:1.

older.title: Relative torsion of the tensor product of block algebras over the PHP algebra (derived tensor products, graded Tor)
older.text: The complete source algebra is the tensor product over the old PHP algebra of the block algebras, none of which is flat; derived tensor products and graded Tor would organise their interaction and locate new z-torsion in the companion ideal. A degree-local relative torsion bound for several blocks would give hardness.
older.reason: Absorbed into the main line: local generation of top syzygies was identified as a Tor group and Taylor glue reduces hardness to Tor vanishing, which is now open statements A2/A3 themselves (a restatement of the open problem, not a separate lead).

older.title: Hopfological algebra of p-complexes (Qi) for the p-nilpotent selector operators
older.text: Selector operators D_l satisfy D_l^p=0 but not D_l^2=0 at odd p, so the obstruction complex is a p-complex with amplitude homology. Qi's hopfological algebra (Khovanov–Qi) treats p-DG modules over F_p[x]/(x^p) with derived categories and Künneth-type results; it could supply exactness and lifting statements for many commuting p-nilpotent operators, the r-parameter lift the p-complex line lacks.
older.reason: Named only as a literature lead and never read; the p-complex line was parked for lack of an r-parameter lift and later returned to as the batched mechanism, so the lead still bears on it.

older.title: Cohomological local-to-global consistency (Ó Conghaile, with Chan–Ng hierarchy lower bounds as controls)
older.text: Organise local moment spaces (local designs on blocks or faces) as a presheaf with restriction maps; Ó Conghaile's cohomological k-consistency detects a Čech-type obstruction to extending compatible local sections, and Chan–Ng's lower bounds show where such algorithms fail. Translated, a global design for PHP plus many clauses would be assembled from local designs on each block's allowed set, with the obstruction class computed explicitly.
older.reason: Partly developed: matching-sheaf-gluing reduced it to an error-cancellation system and restriction-mixture-top-size to a one-count design problem (parked with a restart condition); Ó Conghaile's construction itself was never applied, and A1 now names local designs as the bypass of the union, where this lead bears directly.

older.title: Tseitin inconsistency as a zeroth-homology obstruction
older.text: For an oriented incidence system, solvability of prescribed charges is an image-of-boundary question and total charge per component is the H_0 obstruction; this explains why directly presented linear systems are easy for matching-characteristic algebraic reasoning. Translated, it suggests classifying which clause families have a homological (linear) refutation reason and separating them from those that need degree.
older.reason: Presented as a heuristic comparison and never tested as stated; later Tseitin appearances concern parity literature and onto-graph checks, and the record does not let me decide whether the comparison still bears on an open statement.

older.title: Hyperplane-arrangement complements: topology and finite-field point counts of the false sets
older.text: Full-field false sets of selector clauses are affine arrangement complements; complex arrangement cohomology and finite-field point counts (characteristic polynomial) give invariants of the clause's falsifying set. The translation would need to pass from arrangement data to the Boolean cube and to the degree filtration with original-generator certificates.
older.reason: Untested here (no bridge found in a short screen); later relisted as the Crapo–Rota/Athanasiadis finite-field method, still bearing on the falsifying sets of adversarial blocks. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-26-collective-core-review:2.

older.title: 3-torsion in matching and chessboard complexes (Shareshian–Wachs)
older.text: Integral homology of chessboard complexes has 3-torsion in bottom degrees; if it fell in the range the thread uses, exactness of zero-marginal spaces over F_3 could differ from other fields and affect the odd-prime degree statements.
older.reason: Tested and falsified for the thread's range: the Björner–Lovász–Vrećica–Živaljević connectivity bound makes top cycle spaces field-independent for N>=2t-1, and GAP/HAP found the torsion elsewhere; the separate RSK basis use is tracked as its own later lead.

older.title: Fundamental groups and nonabelian topology of the obstruction complex
older.text: Nonabelian invariants (fundamental groups, nonabelian cohomology) of a complex built from local moment extensions could detect gluing obstructions that linear homology misses. The review ranked them below homology with coefficient systems because the unknowns are linear over a field.
older.reason: Deprioritised without any test and never mentioned again; it is unclear whether a nonabelian invariant has any bearing on the linear gluing problems in the current open statements.
older.open_statement: A1, adversarial forms (gluing of local designs)

older.title: Published bounds on semi-regularity / Fröberg-type behaviour of Boolean quadratic selector systems
older.text: The pause review made a proof or usable published bound for semi-regular or general-position behaviour of Boolean quadratic selector systems modulo PHP a restart condition: it would turn the window heuristics into theorems. Fröberg's conjecture and its proved cases (and Hochster–Laksov) are the outside sources.

older.title: Bounded-depth closure for parity resolution (Byramji–Impagliazzo arXiv 2511.20023; Efremenko–Garlík–Itsykson; Bhattacharya–Chattopadhyay–Byramji) transferred to F_p
older.text: Closure lemmas for parity resolution keep a partial matching consistent with each line's linear system along one path, giving bounds up to depth N^{2-eps} with arbitrary dense lines. An F_p closure lemma for unary PHP plus a path argument would give a bounded-depth Res(lin_F_p) endpoint admitting arbitrarily many window lines.
older.reason: Developed through about a dozen entries (forced-cell, vertex-cover and star closures, modular-collision hardness, walks); the closure-walk review found restrictions blocked and walks capped near the depth floor, concluding the sub-line cannot reach the goal, and it has no bearing on the current PC-degree open statements.

older.title: Distributional analogy: a closure walk absorbs a carried box at linear cost, transferred to design-side certification
older.text: In the closure walk a carried box of forms is absorbed by one batch of swaps at cost linear in its rank, while reweighting by its selector costs degree multiplicatively. Translated, swap-averaged designs might absorb a dense block cheaply.
older.reason: Withdrawn by the correction entry: the walk meets lines one path at a time and pays a union bound, so the analogy transfers the obstruction rather than a mechanism, and the calibration it aimed at was already settled.

older.title: Relative rank and regularization (Lampert–Ziegler), with Janzer and Kazhdan–Ziegler, for a rank-stratified first moment of degree falls
older.text: A degree fall at level B is an element of the degree-B conflict ideal vanishing on the annihilator of the forms, outside the trivial part; a first moment needs a rank of B-forms relative to the ideal and a count of low-rank elements. Lampert–Ziegler's rank relative to a collection of polynomials, combined with Janzer's partition-rank/analytic-rank bound and Kazhdan–Ziegler equidistribution, would supply that relative rank and the high-rank bias bound.
older.reason: Lampert–Ziegler is named once and never read; the degree-three first-moment entry left the Kazhdan–Ziegler exponent question unchecked, and the KZ part was later relisted in killer-moment-review. The relative-rank count still bears on random tops.

older.title: Dade's lemma with Carlson's rank varieties, truncated to degrees at most D
older.text: Over the group algebra of (Z/3)^M, a module is free exactly when it is free over every cyclic shifted subgroup F_3[z]/(z^3), z a generic linear combination of the generators. A truncated version (freeness through degree D from single-element freeness plus Hilbert-series positivity) acting on the row-free model would give the joint many-form lift, that is, row freeness for many selectors at once.
older.reason: Heavily developed (truncated-dade, graded-dade, pencil-graded-dade) and fails in special position, but still listed as continuing in later standard reviews and bears on row freeness, the stated route to W. Deduplicate against entry-2026-09-27-directness-route-review:1 and entry-2026-09-28-coupled-cover-review:2.
older.open_statement: W via row freeness on the allowed set (conj:closed-row-freeness); A1

older.title: Alexander–Hirschowitz theorem and the Horace method (Brambilla–Ottaviani), via Emsalem–Iarrobino apolarity
older.text: By apolarity, degree-3 maximal rank of the selector conditions D_l^2 w = 0 on the matching complex K_3 is a matching-complex analogue of Alexander–Hirschowitz independence of generic double points on cubics. Translate the Horace degeneration: specialize some forms to vanish on one row and run the residual exact sequence relating K_3 of the board to K_3 and K_2 of the board without that row, inducting on n up to the capacity min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)).
older.reason: Developed into row Horace and the pattern-algebra reduction, which stop at the open coupling (C); the capacity-sharp all-n form and higher degrees remain. The idea was carried later as standard items entry-2026-09-27-equivalence-route-review:3 and entry-2026-09-28-ideal-sum-review:1 (dedupe against them).

older.title: Artinian reduction of the chessboard complex's face ring and Hochster's formula (with chessboard connectivity and Shareshian–Wachs torsion)
older.text: If the top algebra G (or a squarefree Gröbner degeneration of it) is an Artinian reduction of a face ring of a chessboard-type complex, Hochster's formula turns Tor vanishing for wide monomial tops into homology vanishing of induced chessboard subcomplexes, where chessboard connectivity and Shareshian–Wachs torsion apply. This targets the width axis (A2) and Tor vanishing for wide tops.
older.reason: Partly developed: the observations entry found Hochster's Tor is a different Tor, and the Gröbner-degeneration entry produced a squarefree complex Delta' for degree 3 only; no wide-top Tor statement followed. Carried later as standard item entry-2026-09-27-designed-line-review:1 (dedupe).

older.title: Lefschetz theorems for Artinian reductions of face rings and the anisotropy method (Adiprasito; Papadakis–Petrotou, odd characteristic)
older.text: Maximal-rank multiplication by squares of forms on G is a Lefschetz-type property; characteristic-p anisotropy gives Lefschetz elements for generic Artinian reductions of face rings of spheres, pseudomanifolds and cycles. A characteristic-3 version adapted to the Frobenius syzygies (l^3 = 0) would supply Tor vanishing in degree for clause tops.
older.reason: Carried in entry-2026-09-25-outside-leads-review and tested in entry-2026-09-27-moment-route-review, which falsified it as a route to the F_3-random statement (generic over a transcendental extension; power-form Lefschetz fails since elements cube to zero). Whether a designed or explicit F_3 use remains is not settled.

older.title: Gröbner and torus degenerations with upper semicontinuity of Tor (the method of the known cases of Fröberg's conjecture)
older.text: Degenerate the algebra G (not the forms) to a monomial or torus-fixed fiber where Taylor resolutions compute Tor, prove vanishing or maximal rank there, and lift it back by semicontinuity. Targets Tor vanishing through degree 22k (A3) and row freeness.
older.reason: Positive at degree 3 (lem:degeneration-transfer), refuted for row freeness because the torus rescales the row sums (degeneration-row-freeness), and falsified for monomial row sums under one order only ("other orders were not searched"). Explicit F_3-rational specializations at higher degree remain untried. Related standard items: fall-tolerance-review:3, row-free-line-review.

older.title: Representation stability for FI-modules (Church–Ellenberg–Farb) for the n to infinity axis
older.text: The map from n to K_t(n) is a functor on injections adding rows and labels; Noetherianity turns vanishing up to the generation degree into vanishing for all n. A fixed tuple of forms breaks the symmetry, so it needs equivariant configurations (orbit specializations) with M growing with n, or symmetry in law as for W_RS random families.
older.reason: Used successfully for the base (thm:tensor-power-freeness via Church–Ellenberg); for forms, falsified for adversarial coefficients (coupling-free review) and left "Not run" for the W_RS failure space, which is symmetric only in expectation (capacity review). The equivariant-family version was never attempted.

older.title: Čech and Leray vanishing on the member cover
older.text: The gluing obstruction is a first Čech group on the cover of the inventory by its members, identified with Tor; a Leray-type theorem would make it vanish when the cover is good, with higher obstructions vanishing on overlaps. Candidate proof strategy for local falls on adversarial families (pencils are bad overlaps).
older.reason: Developed in the cover-gluing entries of 27 September but carried later as standard items entry-2026-09-26-fall-tolerance-review:2 and entry-2026-09-28-satisfiable-cover-review:1, whose audits govern it (dedupe).

older.title: Modular representation theory of (Z/3)^M: Dade's lemma, rank and support varieties, Jordan types
older.text: A = F_3[x_1..x_M]/(x_j^3) is the group algebra of (Z/3)^M with x_j = g_j - 1, so G is a representation with each generator acting as 1 + l_j, and Tor vanishing is truncated relative projectivity. Rank/support varieties and Jordan types could certify it beyond single generic elements.
older.reason: Heavily developed later (truncated and graded Dade, Jordan-type entries) and carried as standard items entry-2026-09-25-closure-route-review:1, entry-2026-09-27-directness-route-review:1, entry-2026-09-27-local-independence-review:3 and entry-2026-09-28-coupled-cover-review:2 (dedupe).

older.title: Fröberg's conjecture: semi-regularity of squares of generic forms in G
older.text: Tor vanishing through B means G/(l_j^2) has its expected Hilbert function through B, a Fröberg-type semi-regularity statement on the injective side, far below capacity. Proofs of the known cases (specialization plus openness, witness families) are the template for A3.
older.reason: Carried later as standard items entry-2026-09-27-survival-review:1 and entry-2026-09-27-convergence-review:2 (dedupe); A3 remains open at logarithmic degree.

older.title: Tropical leading weights with ties (extending lem:tropical-leading-bound)
older.text: Assign tropical weights to cells so that the leading matrix of the double-point map is computable; tie-free weights cap at M(gamma_1-2), so use weights with ties and a second-order leading matrix to reach min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)) on the pattern algebra for every n.
older.reason: Developed into thm:tetrahedral-double-points (about n^3/1330 explicit selectors at degree 3, every n); the capacity-sharp form is paused at the coupling, and whether tied weights extend beyond degree 3 or to wide tops was not tried.

older.title: Gale duality for the column model (squares of Gale-dual linear forms)
older.text: Freeness of a column span in the column model equals the Hilbert function of Sym(V)/(m_1^2..m_n^2) with m_j the Gale transform of the hole-value configuration, a Fröberg/Alexander–Hirschowitz question for a specific point configuration. Locate the special position of the Gale points in the defective degree-4 and degree-5 configurations to decide column freeness.
older.reason: Partly developed (frobenius-class-apolarity handles the characteristic-3 apolarity), but the proposed special-position analysis of defective Gale configurations was not found later; column freeness at density one half is still conjectured in W.

older.title: Razborov's PC degree lower bound for PHP and its description of the PHP ideal, for base stability (a)
older.text: Read Razborov's analysis to prove that weak unary PHP alone has no fall below logarithmic degree, hypothesis (a) of relative gluing.
older.reason: Hypothesis (a) was settled at logarithmic degree (thm:weak-base-stability-quadratic, tensor-power freeness), so the lead has no remaining target.

older.title: Constant Jordan type theory (Carlson–Friedlander–Pevtsova) for truncated freeness of tensor powers
older.text: Modules whose restrictions to all lines have the same Jordan type; their generic-kernel or tensor-product results might give truncated freeness for tensor powers of u(W)/m^2, the if-half of conj:column-tensor-power-freeness.
older.reason: Superseded: thm:tensor-power-freeness proved the conjecture at p = 3 by peeling and FI-modules. Jordan-type ideas for other targets are carried by later standard items.

older.title: Family-dependent substitution in the style of the Weak Rank Principle (Garlík, Gryaznov, Ren, Tzameret, arXiv 2608.08760)
older.text: Find a substitution, depending on the family, that sends each W clause (1-L_i^2) prod L_j^2 into the PHP ideal at logarithmic degree, as Y := X^T A sends rank constraints into degree-2 consequences of functional PHP before Razborov's bound applies.
older.reason: Developed (dense-axiom literature, composition collapse, weak-rank selectors, base selectors) and carried as standard item entry-2026-09-26-thread-review-4:3, whose audit governs (dedupe); base selectors left a corollary with expensive selectors not pushed to a bound.

older.title: Pseudo-calibration for many random dense constraints (Ghosh, Jeronimo, Jones, Potechin, Rajendran, arXiv 2009.01874)
older.text: Build pseudo-expectations or designs by matching low-degree moments of a planted distribution, as done for SoS with polynomially many random dense constraints. Here the target is a Nullstellensatz design on the allowed set for random-prefix families.
older.reason: Dismissed in the review by a one-step objection (adversarial forms break it); later reviews raised it repeatedly and it is carried as standard item entry-2026-09-28-certificate-halves-review:1 (dedupe).

older.title: Symmetric-system lower-bound methods (Potechin–Grigoriev; Hakoniemi, Limaye and Tzameret functional lower bounds)
older.text: These methods prove degree lower bounds by exploiting the symmetry of the whole system. W_RS families are invariant in law under permutations of pigeons and holes, so a symmetrized design (averaging a candidate over the group action) or an expected-case version might apply to random-prefix families even though a fixed adversarial family is not symmetric.
older.reason: Closed only by the one-step objection that an adversarial family breaks symmetry; no entry tried the symmetry-in-law version for W_RS.

older.title: Closure of linear forms (Efremenko–Itsykson amortized closure; Efremenko–Garlík–Itsykson; Bhattacharya–Chattopadhyay; Byramji–Impagliazzo)
older.text: Closure operators handle dense linear forms natively for regular or bounded-depth Res(+). An F_3 analogue for regular or bounded-depth Res(Lin_F3) on PHP plus dense blocks would be an intermediate target and a possible batched mechanism.
older.reason: Read in the source later (ordered closure: not span-invariant over F_3; parity literature); the closure sub-line is parked as weak, but whether a regular-fragment version at odd p was attempted is unclear.

older.title: Part's subset-sum bounds in Res(lin_F_q) via code distance (arXiv 2202.08214)
older.text: Dense linear inputs handled through code distance, for characteristic at least 5 and a restricted fragment.
older.reason: The Boolean-linear entry read the source and found it covers a weak regular fragment splitting on variables, for linear systems not PHP, and W_RS clauses are subspace avoidances, not linear systems.

older.title: Wilson's mod-p inclusion-matrix rank theorem, in a several-form version
older.text: Column Wilson gives Taylor generation for one sparse clause at every degree; a mod-p rank theorem for several set systems at once would give Taylor generation for many clause tops, including the Koszul range and overlapping supports.
older.reason: Taken as the main line: several-form Wilson, column-disjoint Taylor, bounded clusters and conj:two-form-wilson-taylor; designed families are settled, while the block-line review found no local-to-global principle for many forms. It now lives as route conjectures rather than a lead.
